messages:
Jon P.: quick question — after the KY incident i was re-reading the lease-swap logic for tenant residency. is the current handshake sufficient to prevent transient cross-region writes for EU tenants?
Maria L.: we saw one case in staging where both nodes accepted a write during a ~700ms window. not huge but regulatory teams 👀
Miguel R.: idea: explicit quiesce window + txn watermark check on the incoming standby. primary marks transfer_start, then waits for in-flight watermark to be acked, then emits transfer_commit. standby only accepts writes after it sees transfer_commit and confirms residency token.
Anna S.: important constraint: for EU-resident tenants we can’t route writes outside eu-west1 even transiently. that means any quiesce that buffers writes must keep them inside-region (durable queue) or reject. buffering to us-east is a non-starter.
Sam K.: +1 on residency token. handshake should carry: {tenant_id, residency_scope, transfer_id, last_seen_op_ts}. target node verifies policy before responding can_accept=true. also emit audit event with transfer_id.
infra-bot: deploybot: canary deploy started for handshake/fallback-v2 -> canary group (eu-west1)
Jon P.: rough pseudocode for the handshake i sketched this morning:
```
# primary
emit transfer_start(transfer_id, last_op_ts)
wait until last_op_ts_has_committed()
emit transfer_commit(transfer_id)
# standby
on transfer_start -> validate residency_scope
on transfer_commit -> if residency_ok and kv_watermark >= last_op_ts: can_accept=true
```
Maria L.: edge case: what if standby's KV cache has an older value for a hot prefix and serves a stale read right after accept? ops suggestion: flush affected prefixes on commit or force cache rehydrate on first write.
Miguel R.: flush on commit seems ok but expensive for big tenants. alternative: mark prefixes "read-only until rehydrated" and fail fast for writes that would be inconsistent with last_op_ts. tests needed.
Anna S.: legal follow-up: if we have a transient in-region durable buffer, fine. if we drop to a write-reject, customers must see clear 409/429 and reason code. we need copy-ready messaging for SDKs.
Sam K.: add idempotency keys to the buffered writes to avoid dupes if replay occurs during handoff. also ensure we incrementally reconcile ledger on first successful commit.
Maria L.: i'll add a short section to the chaos test matrix: inject handshake delay, simulate kv-stale, simulate region-policy mismatch. we saw the kv-stale only when TTL > 60s in staging.
Miguel R.: ops/runbook items: 1) force cache flush command (api) 2) transfer audit event visible in console 3) automated rollback if can_accept not observed in X ms 4) post-handoff verification probe that reads known marker key.
Jon P.: putting action items together: open RFC follow-up with: handshake v2 design (residency token + transfer_id), buffering guidance (in-region durable queue or reject), cache-flush patterns, idempotency requirements, chaos tests, runbook updates. tagging @Anna S. for regulatory sign-off and @infra-bot for canary status updates.
Anna S.: on it — i'll review the draft and list tenants where "no-transit" policy applies.
Sam K.: can we add an invariant checker in the control plane that prevents transfer_commit when residency_policy disallows target? that would save a lot of manual screwups.
Miguel R.: yes, that should be a gate: control-plane validates policy before allowing transfer_start to progress to commit.
Jon P.: cool. thanks all. i'll capture notes in RFC follow-up and add the checklist. feel free to DM if i missed anything. :thumbsup:
